To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
general skills were positively associated with patient experiences of change and that technical skills showed mixed associations with patient experiences.

the general therapy skills feedback and understanding were associated with the patient experience of change in self-esteem, whereas the technical therapy skill guided discovery was negatively associated with the patient experiences of change in the alliance, contentment and control.

general therapy skills, such as empathy and feedback, explained 23.1% of the variance in patients' self-esteem experiences, whereas the technical skill of guided disovery consistently explained 10.2% to 12.6% of the variance for patients' mastery, clarification, alliance, contentment and control experiences.
